seoTitle: Password Protect PDF Online - AES-256 Encryption, No Upload
metaDescription: Add a password to a PDF with AES-256, AES-128 or RC4-128 encryption and permission flags for print, copy and edit. Done in your browser, nothing is uploaded.
intro: Encrypt a PDF so it asks for a password to open, and set what readers may do with it. The password never leaves your browser.
why:
Sending a contract, a payslip or a scan by email is easier when the file asks for a password. This tool applies the PDF standard security handler: AES-256 (revision 6, the modern default), AES-128 or the old RC4 128-bit scheme for very old readers.

The user password is what a reader types to open the file. The owner password controls the permission flags: printing, copying text, editing and annotating. Leave the owner password blank and a random one is used, which makes the flags impossible to lift with a password but does not stop software that simply ignores them. Honest limit: permission flags are advisory. A viewer that respects them will block printing; a tool that does not will not. Only the open password is real protection.

You can leave the open password empty to set restrictions only. There is no recovery: if you lose the password, the file cannot be opened. The encryption itself runs in your browser with platform crypto APIs; the file and the password are never uploaded.
howTo: Choose a PDF that is not already encrypted.
Type the password needed to open it and, optionally, a separate owner password.
Pick AES-256 unless you need an older reader, and tick or untick the permissions.
Download the protected file and test it by opening it with the password.

faq.a: AES-256 is the strongest and is understood by current viewers (Acrobat, Preview, Chrome, Firefox, poppler, MuPDF). AES-128 works with readers from about 2005. RC4-128 is only there for very old software and is weak.
No. They are a request to the viewer. Many tools ignore them, and anyone who can open the file can usually remove them. Use the open password for real protection.

faq.q: How strong is the password protection?
faq.a: The encryption is sound, the weak point is the password. For AES-256 the password is hashed with the iterated ISO 32000-2 algorithm, but a short or common password can still be guessed. Use a long passphrase, for example from the password generator.

faq.q: Can I protect a file that is already encrypted?
faq.a: Not directly. Remove the old password first, then protect again. This avoids mixing up two passwords.

faq.q: What happens to signatures, forms and bookmarks?
faq.a: Forms, bookmarks and links are kept. The file is rewritten, so any digital signature becomes invalid. Metadata is encrypted too.
